long_biography.plain_text:
Negotiating Capital Group through the 2008 property crash became one of Pavel Tyo's defining acts as a developer. As sales collapsed and lenders pressed for repayment, he spent months working with Sberbank on a restructuring that kept construction moving. The company met its revised obligations and retained its core development platform.

Tyo had joined Capital Group as a shareholder in 1993, taking responsibility for project approvals and relations with Moscow's construction authorities. When his original partners stepped back from operations two decades later, he assumed control of new projects. He refreshed the management team, gave minority stakes to two senior executives and continued to coordinate the group as board chairman.

uncertainties.detail: The Russian surname Тё appears in English as Tyo in the immutable record and some official English news items, Te on the subject's official English personal site, and Tio in some reference sources. These are transliterations of the same Korean-Russian surname. The dossier preserves the immutable Pavel Tyo display name and notes the official Pavel Te form without proposing a name correction.

Forbes Russia reported an 80% holding in 2020 after two senior managers received minority stakes. A current Vedomosti company directory identifies Tyo as the beneficiary and principal shareholder, while Capital Group continues to call him founder and chairman. Because no current primary-source percentage was found, the biography uses principal shareholder but omits a percentage.

Strong sources establish that Tyo worked as an engineer and trader before building Capital Group with partners and do not identify an inherited core asset. They do not establish his family's financial position or the complete funding of his entry well enough to distinguish an independent from an advantaged start, so the broad Self-made classification is retained.

The immutable Russian nationality is consistent with the public record. Korean describes his heritage, while a South Korean citizenship claim appears only in secondary reference material and was not independently confirmed by a sufficiently strong source. No secondary-nationality proposal is made.

The dedicated personal website and official company domain clear the import threshold. The existing LinkedIn URL matches the name, company and Moscow geography but is not linked from either official site and carries sparse activity, so it is preserved as immutable input rather than re-proposed. No exact personal Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube or TikTok account was verified above threshold.

No current vessel fact was used. Private homes and family circumstances, sanctions, politics, legal matters, allegations, controversy, current project forecasts, point-in-time revenue and sales figures, and the older ownership percentage were excluded from the biographies.
